newsitem.title: USA: Jackson said considering third run for presidency.
newsitem.headline: Jackson said considering third run for presidency.

text.p: Civil rights leader Jesse Jackson, unhappy with the White House, is weighing a third run for the presidency in 2000 and is already busy courting an unlikely new soul-mate, Republican House Speaker Newt Gingrich, Time magazine reported Saturday.
Time said the unlikely allies have spoken a few times by telephone. They have been "communing since Gingrich's opening day speech to the House (in January)."
It said Gingrich last week invited Jackson to sit in the Gingrich family box in the Speaker's gallery when President delivers his State of the Union speech Tuesday.
Time quoted an unnamed longtime friend and campaign adviser of Jackson's as saying: "I've never seen him so serious so soon about running."
Jackson ran for the Democratic presidential nomination in 1984 and in 1988.
